chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, is not a tyrant to His servants, nor unaware of them, nor incapable regarding them, nor ignorant of their conditions, nor unaware of their deeds, nor unaware of their intentions, nor unaware of their purposes, nor unaware of their secrets, nor unaware of their outward appearances, nor unaware of their inward states, nor unaware of their hearing, nor unaware of their sight, nor unaware of their hearts, nor unaware of their souls, nor unaware of their bodies.

key_terms.ظَلَّامٍ: Tyrant or one who does injustice

ai.seo_question: What attributes of God's knowledge are mentioned in this hadith from Kamal al-Din?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to underscore the doctrine of *Ilm al-Imam* (the Imam's comprehensive knowledge), illustrating how the divine attribute of omniscience is reflected in the Prophet and Imams. By detailing the spectrum from hidden intentions to outward deeds, the text reinforces the Shia belief in the infallible awareness of the Ahl al-Bayt as the perfect mirrors of God's attributes. This serves as a theological foundation for the Imam's role as the ultimate judge of human sincerity and action.
